3.q: Give the correct order of events in the stream of consciousness when a student absorbs herself in the textbook during a lecture.
3.a: The stream runs: (1) The lecture voice occupies the focus of consciousness at first (2) Interest shifts and the textbook becomes the new focus (3) The teacher's words recede into the fringe of awareness (4) Five minutes pass unnoticed because the stream kept flowing while selection amplified one current. A wrong answer that says she blocked out or paused the noise shows the student has missed that consciousness is continuous and attention is selective amplification, not a switch.

6.q: Give the correct order of elements in a case vignette that demonstrates reaction formation convincingly.
6.a: The vignette runs: (1) Show the unconscious impulse of hostility toward the newborn sibling (2) Display the conscious behaviour of exaggerated doting and constant hugging (3) Mark the exaggeration that goes beyond normal affection and worries the parents (4) Read the rigidity and excess as the defence that hides the opposite feeling. A wrong answer that describes simple kindness or open jealousy shows the student has missed that reaction formation is the exaggerated opposite of the repressed impulse.

5.q: Give the correct order of steps explaining how two honest witnesses can report opposite details of the same argument.
5.a: The explanation runs: (1) Both students encode the same fragmentary events of the quarrel (2) Each carries a different schema about which classmate is the angry one (3) At recall the schema fills the ambiguous gaps with expected details (4) The two reconstructions contradict each other although neither witness is lying. A wrong answer that calls one witness dishonest shows the student has missed that memory is a schema-guided reconstruction rather than a playback of stored facts.

2.q: Give the correct order of points showing why a first-letter sentence is a poor mnemonic for the PQRST method itself.
2.a: The critique runs: (1) The first-letter sentence encodes only initial sounds at a shallow level (2) PQRST is a conceptual procedure whose steps carry meanings (3) Shallow encoding cannot support flexible application of the steps (4) A deeper strategy that processes each step's purpose suits this material better. A wrong answer that praises the sentence for preserving order alone shows the student has missed that levels of processing decide whether the mnemonic actually fits the material.
